clue.text: Fail to make a lot of money

definitions.meaning: a show or venture that flops completely is said to do this, in British usage
in British slang a hit show can also do this, meaning to earn a fortune

explanation.surface: Someone frets that a business plan will not bring in much cash.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word has opposite senses on either side of the Atlantic and in different idioms: a total flop, and (in Britain, 'cost a bomb', 'make a bomb') a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang verb with contradictory senses: to flop badly, and to earn a fortune quickly.

clue.text: Film star, type to get Oscar

parts.note: a brand is a type or make of goods
Oscar is the radio alphabet word for the letter O

explanation.surface: An actor of a certain kind is tipped to win an Academy Award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' looks like the Academy Award in a film clue, but it is just the radio alphabet's O.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlon Brando was a Hollywood actor famous for On the Waterfront and The Godfather.

clue.text: Extra large mushroom

parts.note: extra means more, additional
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A forager has found an enormous fungus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extra large' reads as one size label (XL) describing the mushroom, but the two words are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An edible fungus with a honeycombed cap, prized in cooking.

clue.text: He's a nut, it's turned out

definitions.text: He's a nut, it's turned out

indicators.note: turned out suggests the letters of the preceding words have been turned about into a new order

parts.note: every letter of these words, including both S's, is used

explanation.surface: Someone reveals, a little surprised, that a man is crazy about something.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition: a nut is a fan, so the man described is exactly the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A nut is slang for a keen devotee, as in 'football nut', which is what a fan or zealot is.

clue.text: Welsh name adopted by many Englishmen

indicators.note: adopted by signals letters taken in by the words that follow, sitting across the join between them

explanation.surface: Lots of English people have taken on a name from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'maNY Englishmen'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Welsh short form of Aneurin, as borne by the Labour politician Aneurin Bevan.

clue.text: Heavenly food stored in building near river? That's typical of us

indicators.note: near places the river right beside the building in a down answer
stored in means one piece is kept inside another, so the food goes within the building

parts.note: a hut is a simple building
manna was the food sent from heaven to the Israelites in the Bible
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a common crossword river

explanation.surface: Picture divine sustenance kept in a riverside shed, then a remark that this is just how people are.
explanation.walkthrough: The URE is a river in North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: The traits common to all people are what make behaviour typical of us as a species.

clue.text: Pile of small stones not quite enough for protection

indicators.note: not quite enough says the word falls just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a screen gives protection, as from wind or view

explanation.surface: A heap of pebbles would not shield anyone sufficiently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite enough' trims the last letter, N, from SCREEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose broken rock gathered on a mountain slope is this kind of debris.

clue.text: Building in Oxford could become Alan's home

indicators.note: could become shows the letters that follow may turn into something else when rearranged

parts.note: both the name and its S are used
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Oxford building might one day be converted into a man's house.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashmolean is the university museum of art and archaeology in Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ashmolean Museum in Oxford is Britain's oldest public museum, a notable building there.

clue.text: Live expert turns up in pilot TV programme

indicators.note: in puts the live wire and the expert inside the pilot

parts.note: a pilot scheme is a test run
L is the abbreviation for live, as on electrical wiring

indicators.note: turns up in a down clue means this word is written bottom to top

parts.note: an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: An experienced performer is filmed live for the trial episode of a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' writes the expert's word upwards, as a down answer reads; 'in' then puts it, after the live letter, inside the pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcast on television is a show transmitted to viewers.

clue.text: Newspaper article on immoral behaviour round centre of Stoke

indicators.note: on in a down clue places the first piece above the next

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: round means the wrongdoing encloses the letter from Stoke

parts.note: vice is immoral behaviour

indicators.note: centre of picks out the middle letter of the word Stoke

explanation.surface: A tabloid runs a scandal story about sin centred on a Potteries town.
explanation.walkthrough: The Voice is a British weekly paper serving the Black community.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-running British weekly aimed at Afro-Caribbean readers, a news publication.

clue.text: Officer, I fear, worried about foreign character sounding warlike

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters wrap round the Greek letter
worried suggests the letters of 'I fear' are agitated into a new order

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet, a foreign character

indicators.note: sounding says the word for warlike is heard, not seen, giving a near-identical spoken form

parts.note: martial means warlike

explanation.surface: A nervous commander frets about some outsider who sounds belligerent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges I FEAR; 'about' wraps that round the Greek letter; 'sounding' swaps the word for warlike for one said the same. The rank is the RAF's second highest.
explanation.definitionFit: The second-highest rank in the Royal Air Force, held by a very senior officer.

clue.text: Film heavily criticised in review: cut out first bit of reel?

indicators.note: review read as re-view, looking again the other way, so the word for criticised is read backwards

parts.note: reviled means heavily criticised

indicators.note: cut out first bit of means the opening letter is removed from the word for reel

parts.note: a reel is a Scottish dance

explanation.surface: A movie gets panned by a critic, who suggests the opening of a spool be removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in review' is read as re-view, looking back, so the criticism word runs backwards; 'cut out first bit of' beheads the dance, a reel being a lively Scottish dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliverance is the 1972 John Boorman thriller about a canoe trip.

clue.text: Team player is to fix complaint received by personnel dept

parts.note: to rig is to fix dishonestly

indicators.note: received by means the ailment is taken in by the department

parts.note: HR, human resources, is the personnel department
a twinge is a sharp pain, a minor complaint

explanation.surface: Someone is going to sort out a grievance passed on by the office in charge of staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' reads as a grievance to HR, but it is an ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: A footballer or hockey player on the right flank of a side is a member of the team.

clue.text: Large whale caught by men

indicators.note: by means beside, so the letter sits next to the men

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers or men
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Fishermen land a huge sea creature.
explanation.walkthrough: An orc is an old word for a killer whale or similar sea monster.
explanation.definitionFit: Orc is an archaic name for the orca or another large marine beast.

clue.text: Providing French wine during concert

indicators.note: during means the wine comes in the middle of the concert

parts.note: a gig is a pop concert
vin is French for wine

explanation.surface: Someone supplies Bordeaux to the audience at a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Providing and giving both mean supplying something to someone.

clue.text: Trendy business leader finally ruined, we hear? Wrong

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy
Co is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word leader
we hear says the word for ruined is taken as spoken, giving its sound

parts.note: wrecked means ruined

explanation.surface: Gossip has it that a fashionable company boss ended up broke, which is false.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives R from 'leader'; 'we hear' turns WRECKED into its sound, spelt RECT here.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mistaken or untrue is not right, i.e. in error.

clue.text: Begin to deal with speech

definitions.meaning: to tackle a problem, set about it
a formal talk given to an audience

explanation.surface: A speaker starts on a topic in a talk.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means tackle an issue; as a noun, a formal oration to an audience.

clue.text: Note advertisements are cut at start and end of midday TV broadcast

parts.note: D is a musical note
ads is short for advertisements

indicators.note: cut means the word are loses its final letter
at start and end of takes the first and last letters of midday

explanation.surface: Someone says commercials were trimmed from a lunchtime show.
explanation.walkthrough: Dad's Army is a classic British sitcom about the wartime Home Guard, still repeated on TV.
explanation.definitionFit: A much-repeated BBC comedy series, a programme broadcast on television.

clue.text: Rent flat in Channel Island for school holiday

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters inside the island

parts.note: Herm is one of the small Channel Islands

indicators.note: rent as torn means the word flat is ripped apart and rearranged

explanation.surface: An apartment is let on a small island off France for the break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like letting property, but means torn. Herm is a tiny island near Guernsey; half-term is a short break mid-way through a British school term.
explanation.definitionFit: A short break in the middle of a British school term, usually a week.

clue.text: Coin, one kept by an old fellow

indicators.note: kept by means the numeral is held inside the coin

parts.note: a cent is a coin
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A penny is held onto by an elderly man.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient as a noun is an old word for an aged man, as in the ancients of a village.

clue.text: Stash of money fellow mislaid? One's ruined

indicators.note: mislaid means the fellow's letter has been lost from the fund

parts.note: a fund is a stock of money
one, with the 's read as is

explanation.surface: A man has lost his savings and so is done for.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly the 's means 'is' and links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To be undone is to be brought to ruin, an old literary sense.

clue.text: A posh female's taped new Robbie Williams hit

indicators.note: taped as bound round means the new letter is wrapped inside

parts.note: gel is an upper-class pronunciation of girl; the possessive gives the S

explanation.surface: An upper-class woman has recorded a fresh song by a pop star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taped' looks like recording, but means wrapped round. Angels was a 1997 hit for the singer Robbie Williams.
explanation.definitionFit: Angels was Robbie Williams' signature 1997 single.

clue.text: Mostly hard wood

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, losing its final letter

parts.note: firm means hard

explanation.surface: Timber that is largely tough.
explanation.definitionFit: Timber from a conifer tree is a common softwood.

clue.text: Drivers wanting motorway to go through Newhaven? It's preposterous

definitions.note: a plural for a singular type, the stereotype standing for all such drivers

indicators.note: to go through means the motorway is set inside the rearranged letters
preposterous means absurd, so the letters are thrown into nonsense order

parts.note: the Sussex ferry port name plus the pronoun, the 's read as is
M stands for motorway, as in M1

explanation.surface: Locals react to plans for a motorway through a Sussex port town as absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'preposterous' scrambles NEWHAVEN and IT; 'to go through' puts the motorway's M inside. As printed Newhaven has an E where an A is needed, the setter's slip. White van man is the British stereotype of the brash van driver.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase stereotypes a class of brash van driver, so it stands for such motorists collectively.

clue.text: Beef and drink to accompany it, you say?

indicators.note: you say tells the solver the drink's name is heard, giving a word spoken the same

parts.note: red wine is the drink that goes with roast beef

explanation.surface: Someone asks what to serve with a joint of roast meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beef' is a noun in the surface, but the definition is the verb: to complain.
explanation.definitionFit: To beef, in slang, is to complain or grumble.

clue.text: Sect member sounds crazy

indicators.note: sounds says the name of the cult follower is heard, giving a word spoken identically

parts.note: a Moonie is a member of the Unification Church founded by Sun Myung Moon

explanation.surface: A cult follower comes across as mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Moony is informal for dreamy or daft, a little mad.

clue.text: Wasting time in equestrian sport, prissy girl makes a bloomer

indicators.note: wasting means the time letter is thrown away from the sport

parts.note: eventing is a horse-riding competition
prim means prissy
Rose is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A fussy young woman makes a blunder at a horse trials event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a mistake, but means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellow-flowered plant opening in the evening is a flowering plant, a bloomer.

clue.text: Was in control of country, leader having been deposed

indicators.note: leader having been deposed means the first letter of the country is dropped

parts.note: Iran is a country

explanation.surface: Someone governed a nation until a coup ousted its head.
explanation.definitionFit: To have run something is to have managed or been in charge of it.

clue.text: French president once given hand with mission

indicators.note: with joins the hand to the mission, side by side

parts.note: mitt is slang for a hand
an errand is a mission or task

explanation.surface: A former head of state in Paris is given a job and a helping hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Francois Mitterrand was President of France from 1981 to 1995.

clue.text: A word of agreement, or several

definitions.text: A word of agreement, or several

parts.note: yes is the word of agreement

explanation.surface: A dictionary-style note on a word for assent and its plural.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as A YES it is one word of agreement; as a single word it is the plural of aye, several such words.
explanation.definitionFit: Votes in favour in Parliament are counted as these, plural of the assent word aye.
